utterances.text: You have questions?

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Oh, you're saying because while we have quorum.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: I'm good.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You got it.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'll now turn it over to Councilmember Morano, followed by Wong.

chapters.summary: Morano asks how DOF arrived at the $25 million budget projection and what participation rate it requires. Lee says it is an initial projection that will be updated, and notes DOF traditionally collects $75-80 million annually, with $88 million collected in FY2026.
chapters.title: Morano questions the $25 million revenue projection

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Commissioner, one thing that jumped out at me after seeing your testimony,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: is the adopted budget assumes $25 million from this program.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: How did you arrive at $25 million?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if that's a conservative estimate, a target, or something else.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: It's an initial projection.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: It's an initial projection of what is anticipated from this program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: But as we go through the program, those revenue figures will be updated by the time we get through, like, November, preliminary and executive plans.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So what participation rate does that assumption require?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We can get back to you on that one, on the participation rate.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So one distinction I'd like to understand of that projected $25 million, how much represents money you believe the city would have collected anyway without amnesty?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We can follow up on those figures right now.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Besides the $25 million, so including the $25 million, we have currently projected $100.76 million, right?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So traditionally, we are collecting just around the $75 to $80 million mark.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: For 2006, we collected $88 million.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So it is in line with our past collection efforts.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: 26 was at $88 million.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So it is above what we normally collect.

chapters.summary: Morano asks how DOF will verify corrections before granting financial benefits and whether someone could receive the discount first and fail to correct afterward. Lee confirms the issuing agency certifies compliance and that compliance must occur before amnesty is granted.
chapters.title: Morano asks about compliance verification before granting amnesty

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I was very pleased to see in your testimony that violations requiring correction actually have to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I think that's an important safeguard, and I'm glad that it's in there.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: How will the Department of Finance verify the correction before granting the financial benefit?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Are you relying on the issuing agency to certify the compliance, or is there something else?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes, it is the issuing agency that we'll be working with in terms of compliance.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And it is a program you have to...

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Comply in order to receive the program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So it is a specific thing that we have.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So could you have a situation, and it sounds like the answer is no, but I just want to be clear, where somebody receives the discount first and

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: and then fails to complete the correction afterward, or must compliance occur before the amnesty is granted?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: They have to comply first.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Gotcha.

chapters.summary: Morano notes that excluding idling violations because recipients are logistics companies implies need is a factor, and asks why that principle isn't applied more broadly to differentiate between multinational corporations and small businesses. Lee explains various exclusion categories but says the program is applied equally across eligible violations.
chapters.title: Morano questions idling exclusion and need-based relief principle

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: My last question.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You execute, in your testimony, you specifically say that idling violations are excluded because you guys want to hold bad actors accountable.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So you exclude idling violations partly because the recipients tend to be logistics companies that you say are less in need of amnesty.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So need is apparently a factor in deciding who gets relief.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If that's the case, why not apply that principle more broadly?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Why should a multinational corporation and a neighborhood pizzeria receive the same percentage reduction?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So there are a number of reasons why a entity might not be able to participate in the program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: If it was included in an agreement with, let's say, this sheriff's office or city marshal before court counsel, or an execution has been issued before...

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Upon the sheriff's office or violation being converted to tax lien or violation subject to criminal investigation, there are a number of violations that will not be participating in the ECB amnesty program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Idling is one of the ones.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: that will not be participating in the MNC program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Councilmember Wong.

chapters.summary: Wong notes DOF collected $88 million out of $573 million collectible and asks what contributes to this low rate. Lee explains respondents sometimes cannot be identified or businesses no longer exist, and describes efforts to recategorize uncollectible debt and employ new strategies.
chapters.title: Wong asks about low collection rate and its causes

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Majority leader.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Commissionally, I believe you just testified that in fiscal year 2026, you collected $88 million in ECB debt.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So is it fair to say?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: That out of the $573 million that's potentially collectible, you may only be able to collect $88 million in the coming year without this program?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We are hopeful that it will be greater than that once we build in some of our partnerships.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: With the other city agencies that implement additional strategies.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: But right now, as of 2026, for fiscal year 2026, DOF collected $88 million.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So can you talk about what contributes to this low rate of collection?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Let's not talk about the program for a minute.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Look at your existing issues.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Please talk about why you're only able to collect such a low rate.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And sometimes it's because respondents cannot be identified.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Sometimes it's because respondents no longer exist.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Or businesses no longer exist, we have a period in which we outreach to them, and then we have a period in which our outside collection agencies reach out to them.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: But after that,

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: It is deemed uncollectible.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And so we are right now going back into the uncollectible category to see if it could recategorize as collectible.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And we're trying to increase efforts to do better collections internally by employing new strategies and working with our partner agencies.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So it seems to me outreach is a big issue.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Like for businesses that you no longer hear from.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: It could be a issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: All right.

chapters.summary: Wong asks what stops a repeat offender with multiple default judgments from using the program the same way as someone with one honest mistake, and suggests a hardship standard to separate struggling homeowners from chronic violators. Lee says the program does not differentiate and is applied equally to all eligible violations.
chapters.title: Wong asks about repeat offenders and hardship standards

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Here's my question.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: How could you...

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I'm aware of repeated offenders with several default judgments.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: They're in every district.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: They're certainly in my district, and I know who they are.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So my question is, what is stopping a repeated offender with several default judgments from walking through this program that you're proposing in the exact same way as someone with one honest mistake?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I mean, I don't see...

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Anything in this bill that would distinguish them?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: No, we are not differentiating.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We want to ensure that all respondents have an opportunity to cure their existing violations.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We want better outcomes for individuals and the city.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And so we are not specifically

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: you know, separating or congregating or, you know, doing anything other than implementing a program if a violation is outlawed.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: eligible and to cure the actual violation in hand, then they will be eligible for the amnesty program.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I want to follow up.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Can I have a follow up?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Yeah, your time is still going.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You have more time.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: See, this is what I find disturbing because you're giving people a second chance.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: All right, fine.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: But there shouldn't be some kind of a hardship standard.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So we're not putting struggling homeowners in the same category as a landlord who's racking up violations for years and just decided not to pay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So can you talk about that?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: I mean, we, again, are producing a program in which if the violation is docketed with Department of Finance, then they have an opportunity to cure those violations.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And then receive a portion of their fines reduced.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Right now we are not separating out between bad actors who you might see as bad actors or ones that are getting their judgments for the first time.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We are just implementing a program that's equal across the board so that if you cure your violations, which is the

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: outcome that we're hoping to see here, then you'll be able to reduce your fines.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Narcisse praises DOF's relationship with her office, asks about helping people pay from the start rather than waiting for amnesty, and raises a constituent case of a disabled homeowner whose exemption renewal was allegedly lost. Lee offers to look into the case offline through the tax exemptions unit.
chapters.title: Narcisse discusses early outreach and constituent exemption case

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Narcisse?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Commissioner again, Commissioner Lee.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And I have to start by saying thank you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We have great relationship in my office.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Your agency been coming and I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So I'm not against amnesty.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: As a business person, I love the idea, but I'm thinking.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How we can help folks to pay the bills from the get-go instead of reaching to a point where we have so much money out and then we're trying to hire people, we're trying to get the money, and it's great.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So what really inspired the whole process for us to have that bill in front of us?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Well, so one of the things that we are actually trying to improve is the outreach at the get-go, right?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Instead of waiting, let's say, X amount of weeks, days, weeks, months, we're trying to increase the

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: outreach into the respondents at a very early stage because in the past, it's found that once we reach out to them on the early stages, then they're

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: more highly likely to actually address their violation because it's still very fresh.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So, you know, that is one of the things that we are going to improve over the next couple of years.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: That's actually one very specific thing we're doing.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I love it because once the person, oh, that's the time to catch them and make a deal with them.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I don't like to use that word, but make an arrangement with them.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And so they can pay the bill.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, and that is a change that we are putting in.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm all for that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And I'm hoping that we can come to a point, too, for those folks that are driving in our street to be paying their tickets.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And some of them are plates that I cannot even read myself.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They're missing numbers.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: But that's another story.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We should have that conversation because it's ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Separate from this bill.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And elderly homeowners, I'm taking it to my district, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I mean, in my district, mailed his disabled homeowners exemption renewal in March.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: DOF says he was never received.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We have proof of mailing.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: DOF says it is waiting on the tax commission.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What is the process for restoring his exemption for 2026, 2027?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Because he really in need for it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What can my office do?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, so we're happy to talk offline if you give me the constituent's information.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: It goes through our tax exemptions unit.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And so if you give us this information, we're happy to kind of go back and see what communication, you know, our tax exemption unit should be in conversation.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And I think what's happening is they're trying to challenge the initial judgment from the exemptions, which is what the tax commission is for, right, is to appeal DOF decisions.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So we're happy to take a look offline if you give us the constituent information.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Being a nurse, you know, whenever I have disabled folks and I have a few questions, I'm not going to keep it because I know chair want to finish the time.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: My time is up.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks how much DOF collected in FY2026 and what percentage of ECB judgments are collected through the judgment settlement program. Lee reports $88 million collected and about 33% through the judgment settlement program.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about FY26 collections and judgment settlement program

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Councilwoman.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: In March 2026, DOF announced a 30-day review of its efforts to collect outstanding ECB judgment debt and stated that, as of October 2024,

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Approximately $573 million in ECB judgment debt was identified as potentially collectible, while approximately $744 million was deemed uncollectible.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: DOF also projected collecting $70.1 million in fiscal year 26 and indicated that additional collection efforts could increase collections beyond that amount.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: How much did DOF collect for FY 2026?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So for 26, we ended up collecting $88 million.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: What percentage of the ECB judgments are collected through the judgment settlement program?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Through the judgment settlement program, about a third, 33%.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks whether the $573 million collectible and $744 million uncollectible estimates are still current. Lee confirms those figures remain the current estimates.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about current debt estimates

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Does DOF still estimate that approximately $573 million outstanding judgment debt is potentially collectible and $744 million uncollectible?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If not, what is the department's current estimate?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So that is the current estimate.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And again, debt is considered uncollectible for a number of different reasons, including businesses and respondents who were not able to be identified or contacted.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And again, it could be because businesses went out of business and we are no longer able to.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Contact them and receive these collections.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: So the estimate is about the same still?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: That is our current estimate.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks what criteria DOF uses to deem ECB judgments uncollectible. Deputy Commissioner Hill explains cases that have cycled through all three outside collection agencies without collection, as well as deceased individuals and bankrupt businesses, are considered uncollectible.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about criteria for deeming judgments uncollectible

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: DOF indicated, actually I have another question.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: What are the criteria used by DOF to deem the ECB judgments uncollectible?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Our deputy commissioner can answer our uncollectible.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Categories?

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: Okay, so cases that has gone through three collection agencies, they cycle through all three collection agencies and there's no collection has been done and no information has been gotten on them.

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: Sometimes it involves deceased individuals or people who are bankrupt and the business is no longer operating.

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: Those are what's considered uncollectible.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks about expected revenue from permit enforcement partnerships, lien conversions, and targeted outreach. Lee estimates $10 million from permitting partnerships, $1.5 million from outreach, and says lien conversion estimates are pending discussions with DOB on scope.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about revenue from innovative collection strategies

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: DOF indicated that the department is pursuing innovative and targeted strategies to expand collections, including partnering with the Department of Buildings and the Department of Transportation to enforce license and permit suspensions,

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: requiring licensees and permit holders to satisfy outstanding ECB judgment debt before applying for or renewing credentials.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Two, converting DOB-issued ECB judgments into property liens to strengthen enforcement and improve recovery rates.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And three, implementing targeted outreach efforts, including specialized mailings to encourage payment and increase compliance.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: How much additional revenue does DOF expect each of these initiatives to generate in FY27?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So, again, we are constantly trying to improve and working with our city agencies, sister agencies, in order to improve some of the collections.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And we've been in constant communication with them.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: The efforts that we have with, like, DOT and DOB in terms of, like, permitting, our early estimate is about $10 million.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Our increased outreach efforts we think will yield an additional $1.5 million.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: In terms of the lien conversions, that is something that we are in constant contact with DOB on and a legislative route that we are currently seeing if it's a viable option or not.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So we don't necessarily have an estimate for that, but we are trying to figure out what could be done right now.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And when do you think you can get an estimate on the lean conversions?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We're working with the Department of Buildings on the scope.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: And once you figure out the scope, I think it will give us a better understanding of what is convertible and what's not.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Once you figure out the scope and what makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, like scope of violations, what makes sense, how long, what's dockable, what's not.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Sort of once we get a little bit more into the details with DOB is when we'll figure it out.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And you can share that with us.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Sounds great.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks how DOF defines worst offenders, how many fall into that category, and the total debt associated with them. Lee explains that idling violations, judgments in criminal action, and those with sheriffs or marshals are excluded from amnesty, and DOF can explore additional exclusion categories.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about definition of worst offenders

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The announcement stated that DOF intends to prioritize collection of debt from the city's worst offenders.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: How does DOF define worst offenders?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: How many respondents fall into that category?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And what is the total outstanding ECB judgment debt associated with those respondents?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So worst offenders, we're using a little generally, but the idling violations will not be part of the amnesty program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: I indicated earlier some judgments that are going through, let's say, criminal action or the sheriffs or marshals will not be eligible.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So there are a number of violations that will not be eligible for the ECB amnesty program.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Are you contemplating additional types of respondents that should not be eligible?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: At the moment?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We can look at additional and see if there are additional categories that we can include or exclude, I guess, from the amnesty program.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We're happy to have those conversations.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And it's fair to say those offenders will not be eligible to participate in the amnesty program, correct?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks about DOF collection FTEs and whether the number is sufficient. Deputy Commissioner Hill reports five current staff with plans to reach 12. Lee says DOF will work with available resources and use new staff for one-on-one outreach through the Alternative Enforcement Unit.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about enforcement tools and collection staff sufficiency

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And my last set of questions are on enforcement tools, and then I'll have exhausted my questions, unless someone else has any other questions.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: DOF mentioned the use of several enforcement tools in the past to collect on ECB debt currently.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: How many DOF-employed collection full-time equivalents are on staff?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: The full-time equivalents, could you give that?

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: There are currently five full-time in our account executive unit.

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: As I mentioned before, we have vacancies and postings, so we expect to have 12 by the time we do a hire.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And do you consider that to be a sufficient number?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We're going to work with the resources that we have.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: It is an increase for us, and we're going to use those staff to do the one-on-one expanded sort of outreach, especially for our AEU unit, our alternative enforcement unit,

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: that will talk to and guide the highest violations.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Considering the amount...

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Oh, my volume went up.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: That's why I caught myself in the middle.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: It kind of surprised me.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Considering the amount...

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: the amount of debt outstanding and other resources like the marshals and sheriff's office, I guess I am repeating the question.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Do you feel like you have sufficient DOF collection staff and you say you work with the resources you have?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Spoken like a true politician commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: We believe it is sufficient and we're going to work through and improve all the ECP collections.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: To make them be more respondent.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And I'm sure you can do more with more, right?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: I think everybody would say they can always do more with more.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks how many outside collection agencies are contracted and about the sheriff's action plan for ECB judgments. Lee confirms three outside agencies. Deputy Commissioner Hill explains referrals to legal for marshal execution when bank account information is available.
chapters.title: Abreu asks about outside agencies and sheriff's enforcement plan

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: How many current outside collection agencies are contracted with DOF to collect ECB judgments administered?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: ECB judgments specifically, we have three outside collection agencies.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Can you explain the city sheriff's and deputy's action plan to enforce ECB judgments?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So their action plans to enforce?

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: I don't have an action plan for them, but I will tell you when we will refer.

utterances.speaker: Annette Hill
utterances.text: Once we have information, bank account information, we'll refer them to the legal department for the marshals to do an execution on the outstanding judgment.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right, one last question to wrap up this part of the hearing.

chapters.summary: Wong raises concerns that putting information on a website is insufficient for people who don't check websites and asks whether DOF will proactively reach out to small businesses with outstanding ECB judgments. Lee says DOF will use all forms of outreach to connect with eligible respondents.
chapters.title: Wong asks about proactive outreach to small businesses

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Council Member Wong.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: My last issue is outreach because putting this in a website, you know, is not enough, especially for people that don't check on websites.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: They just automatically, you know, they get automatically deducted from their bank accounts and just get an email.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So my question to you is, will Department of Finance, if this program

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: gets approved, voted on, will Department of Finance proactively reach out to small businesses with these outstanding ECB judgments that may benefit from the program?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: If we have the means to connect.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: With the existing pool of ECB violation individuals, we're more than happy to do that in one form or another.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yes, because as I see it now, they will never know about it.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: They might not know about it, you're right.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: So we will, again, we're going to utilize all forms of outreach in order to get respondents to participate.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Abreu thanks the DOF witnesses and excuses the panel, then opens the floor for public testimony and provides instructions for members of the public on how to testify and submit written statements.
chapters.title: Abreu excuses DOF panel and opens public testimony

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Well, thank you so much, Councilman, and thank you so much, Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This panel is hereby excused.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I now open the hearing of public testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Before we begin, I remind members of the public that this is a formal government proceeding and that the quorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: As such, members of the public shall remain silent at all times.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who wish to testify.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: No video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the sergeant at arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If you wish to speak at today's hearing, please fill out an appearance card with the sergeant at arms and wait for your name to be called.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Once you have been recognized, you will have two minutes to speak on the legislation being considered today.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If you have a written statement or additional written testimony you wish to submit for the record, please provide a copy of that testimony to the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You may also email written testimony to testimony at council.nyc.gov within 72 hours of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Audio and video recordings will not be accepted.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: When you hear your name, please come up to the witness panel.

chapters.summary: Upper West Side resident Sue Peters testifies about the banking system's role in creating money as debt, drawing from her career in data processing at a Wall Street bank, and urges council members to educate themselves and the public about how money creation works.
chapters.title: Public testimony: Sue Peters on banking and money creation

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'll now call on our first panel of witnesses, Susan Peters.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And if anyone else is here to testify, please fill out an appearance card.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I believe you're my constituent, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Peters.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And you may start whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: It's very interesting listening to the position our small business people are in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: It's very tough out there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: And I'm here to talk about why it's tough and also why people on the city council

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: need to educate themselves about why it's so tough for our business people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: My name is Sue Peters, and I'm a resident of the Upper West Side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: I'm glad to be speaking to my local elected officials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: In the last 17 years of my long career in data processing, I worked for a Wall Street bank.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: I discovered through the bookkeeping that I was responsible for what the bank does, the power of the bank.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Quote, every time a bank makes a loan, all it is doing is simply making a bookkeeping entry in the borrower's account for the amount of the loan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: This bookkeeping entry is debt to the borrower and earns interest to the bank, end quote.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: In other words, our money does not come from our government, nor does the bank loan out money from savers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: The bank creates it as debt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: This fact is not taught in our schools or discussed in our media.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Whoever controls the creation of the money of a country controls that nation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Money is power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: We all know that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Why do I bring this to your attention?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Because you were public servants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: And can investigate this and inform the citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Aren't all of us entitled to the truth of our history and the truth of the world we live in?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Only then can we think about how to change our world for the benefit of everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: I'd like to end with a quote from a New York City businessman and author from 1883.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Quote, the most fundamental law in any nation is that which institutes money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: For money governs the distribution of property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: And thus affects in a thousand ways the relations of man to man.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: And I have some, actually four different handouts, you know, for the committee to read.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: And I have

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sue Peters
utterances.text: I have a copy of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Well, thank you so much for testifying, Susan Peters.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And can the sergeant please pass along her papers so we can read it?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you to all of you who came here to, you are excused, my apologies.

chapters.summary: Abreu thanks public witnesses, checks for additional in-person and Zoom testimony, finds none, reminds attendees they can submit written testimony within 72 hours, and concludes the hearing.
chapters.title: Abreu closes hearing with no further witnesses

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you to all of you who came here to share your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If there's anyone in the room who wishes to speak but has not yet had the opportunity to do so, please raise your hand and fill out an appearance card with the sergeant at arms at the back of the room.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Seeing no hands in the committee room, we will now shift to virtual testimony via Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Participants on Zoom, please listen for your name to be called and respond to any prompt to be unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You may begin your testimony after the sergeant at arms starts the clock.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I don't believe there's anyone signed up on Zoom, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We are making a final call for Zoom registrants who have not yet spoken.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Seeing no registrants on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If you are currently on Zoom and wish to speak but have not yet had the opportunity to do so, please use the raise hand function and our staff will unmute you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Again, seeing no hands, I would like to know that everyone can submit written testimony to testimony at

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: council.denyic.gov within 72 hours of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: That concludes our hearing for today.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader and Brian.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: My pleasure.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Anytime for you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Take care.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Bye-bye.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lee
utterances.text: Bye.

summary: Finance Committee holds a hearing on a pre-considered bill (T2026-2303) to establish a temporary ECB Amnesty and Compliance Program, allowing eligible judgment holders to resolve outstanding Environmental Control Board violations at reduced penalties.

DOF Commissioner Richard Lee testifies on the program's design, projected $25M in revenue, exclusion of idling violations, and new enforcement strategies including inter-agency permit partnerships and lien conversions.

Council members question DOF on fairness concerns, prior amnesty program results, collection staff levels, outreach plans, and whether repeat offenders should be treated differently from one-time violators.
title: Committee on Finance
topic: Establish a temporary program to resolve outstanding judgments imposed by the environmental control board
